summary: Investigated user-reported styling regressions and sidebar overflow at min/max sizes after the accessibility/sidebar refactor commit (4a33224). Found one concrete CSS regression — the `[data-screen-open='true'] > :is(...)` direct-child rule no longer matches because panels are wrapped in a `display: contents` div — and one likely geometry bug where the shell's `minmax(0, var(--left-column))` tracks can render narrower than the inline `--sidebar-width` the resize handle and panel content assume, causing detachment at extremes. Stopped short of fixes because the broader 'very off' report is too vague to address blind.
decisions: Treated the direct-child `[data-screen-open='true'] > :is([data-ui='sidebar'], [data-ui='conversation'], [data-ui='inspector'], [data-ui='panel-resize-handle'], [data-ui='drawer-scrim'])` selector in shell-parts/layout.css as broken by the new display:contents wrapper — workspace panels are no longer hidden when a modal screen opens (likely visually masked by the fixed overlay but dead-wrong).

Identified `minmax(0, var(--left-column))` / `minmax(0, var(--right-column))` in the app-shell grid as the suspect for overflow at sidebar min/max: the track can shrink below --sidebar-width under viewport pressure while resize handles and panel content still reference the unscaled inline width.
Chose to ask the user for screenshots (normal view, sidebar at min, sidebar at max) plus a hard reload to rule out stale HMR state in their long-lived incognito window, rather than patching blind.
Verified removed hooks `[data-ui='session-list']`, `[data-ui='section-label']`, `[data-ui='card-label']` no longer appear in markup, so their CSS removal is not the source of styling issues.
errors: User report: app styles look 'very off' at typical viewport size in a long-lived incognito window, plus overflow issues at smallest and biggest sidebar widths. Root cause not isolated — possible stale HMR/module-graph state across dev-server restarts, plus the two code regressions noted above.
